messages:
maria: Thinking about the next model upgrade — can we sketch a canary config that uses fractional/attenuated steps instead of fixed percent jumps? want smaller deltas near SLO boundaries and faster steps when healthy.
elliot: +1. current 'percent-and-wait' feels too coarse. idea: max_delta, min_step, dwell, and an attenuation curve that reduces step size as cumulative error delta increases.
sam: totally. also need a circuit for per-customer quotas so we don't push big customers into degraded paths during early ramps.
kevin: sketching a schema below — very rough YAML to start a conversation. feel free to bikeshed names.
kevin: ```
rollout: 
  strategy: canary
  steps:
    - target_pct: 1
      dwell_s: 1800
    - target_pct: 5
      dwell_s: 3600
  attenuation:
    type: adaptive
    max_delta_pct: 10     # cap on absolute jump per step
    min_step_pct: 0.5     # smallest allowed step
    curve: exponential   # linear | exponential | sigmoid
  guards:
    error_rate_increase: 0.005  # absolute increase that triggers hold
    p95_latency_ms: 1200
    min_samples: 200
  per_customer_override: true
```
maria: I like the min_samples guard. we should make the guards pluggable to support custom eval hooks (e.g., hallucination detector).
elliot: two UX asks: 1) console should show 'next step ETA' and 'max permitted jump' computed from current state and attenuation curve. 2) allow manual step-down (force smaller next jump) from UI.
nash: (prod) — i'm ashley, product — can we avoid exposing curve math in the UI? product wants simple knobs: speed (slow/normal/fast), safety (low/medium/high). backend converts to curve params.
kevin: agreed, map speed->curve and safety->max_delta/min_step. but surface an "advanced" YAML editor for infra teams.
sam: operational concerns: telemetry needs to show cohort-level SLO deltas vs baseline and a cohort weight timeline. also we need a synthetic traffic cohort to speed up telemetry for small-sample customers.
maria: good point. add a synthetic-sample option in rollout config so we can inject canary traffic from internal testers or replay.
elliot: also want automatic attenuation when we see noisy signals: e.g., if p95 jumps but error rate stable, backoff to previous step and increase dwell.
kevin: proposal for simple state machine: PROGRESSING -> HOLD -> ROLL_BACK. transitions driven by guard evaluation window (rolling 5m, 30m).
nash: deployment bot note: deploy-bot: rollout started for model v3.2 on canary % sequence [0.5, 1, 3, 7, 15] dwell=30m max_delta=8%
ci-bot: ci-bot: test-suite: canary-guards passed (smoke + perf). full-e2e queued.
maria: next actions: elliot/kevin, can you draft server-side validation rules for max_delta and min_step? sam/ashley: pick UI knobs mapping and telemetry dashboard tiles. i'll draft a doc with examples and failure-mode diagrams.
kevin: will do. sketching validation: max_delta must be <= 20% unless enterprise_override, min_step >= 0.1% and dwell >= 60s. also enforce monotonic non-decreasing target_pct sequence.
elliot: +1, also require explicit approval when cumulative canary >50% for customer-scoped rollouts.
maria: thanks — let's take this into a short RFC. keep replies short here or add comments on the doc. :thumbsup:
